description_en: This three-bayed Phalcā is located in a narrow street that leads to Lukhusi from Hakatvāḥ and faces east. A statue of Amitābhā (sitting in the ‘meditation gesture’) is placed in a wall. The building's first floor has remarkably carved wooden windows. The inscription recording the initial construction of the Phalcā disappeared from here after it was renovated following the 2015 earthquakes. According toBasukala and Gutschow(2018), the inscription was from 1760 CE. This could be the date of the Phalcā’s initial construction.This Phalcā has aguṭhīmaintained and run by a Śreṣṭha clan living in Sundhara, Patan. Theguṭhīsponsors the distribution ofsamaybajiduring the Indrajātrā Festival from this Phalcā. On that occasion, a Bhairava mask used to be publicly displayed inside the Phalcā and traditional rice beer used to be poured from the Bhairava’s mouth. This tradition was calledHāthu Hāykegu. After this mask was stolen sometime between 1975-1985 CE, the tradition came to an end. However, the yearly distribution ofsamayabjistill takes place from the Phalcā.
description_ne: हकटोलबाट लुखुसि जाने साँघुरो बाटो किनारामा यो फल्चा अवस्थित छ । पूर्वाभिमुख दुई तले फल्चाको भूमि तल्ला तीन कवलमा बनेको छ । फल्चाको भित्तामा अमिताभको मूर्ति ध्यान मुद्रामा बसेको मूर्ति टाँसिएको छ । फल्चाभन्दा माथिको तल्लामा कलात्मक काष्ठझ्यालहरू हालिएको छ । यो फल्चाको निर्माणसंग सम्बन्धित शिलापत्र विगत फल्चामा हुने गर्दथ्यो । सन् २०१५ को भूकम्प पछि गरिएको पुनःनिर्माण पश्चात् उक्त शिलापत्र फल्चाबाट हराएको छ ।Basukala and Gutschow(2018) का अनुसार उक्त शिलापत्र सन् १७६० को हो जसमा फल्चको निर्माण मिति र निर्माताका बारे लेखिएको थियो ।यस फल्चासंग सम्बन्धित पाटन, सुन्धाराका श्रेष्ठ खलकको गुठी छ । उक्त गुठीले वार्षिक इन्द्रजात्राको समय यस फल्चामा बसी समय्‌बजि वितरण गर्ने परम्परा चलाउँदै आएको छ । उक्त दिन विगतमा भैरवको मुखाकृति प्रदर्शनमा राखी भैरवको मुखबाट छ्याङ् प्रवाह गर्ने (हाथु हाय्‌केगु) परम्परा पनि अस्तित्वमा थियो । सन् १९७५-१९८५  को बीचमा प्रदर्शनमा राखिने उक्त भैरव मूर्ति चोरी भए पश्चात् समय्‌बजि वितरण मात्र गर्ने गरिएको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: The Phalcā was constructed in 1760 CE.
The Phlacā was rebuilt by the joint effort of local people and the then Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan City.
The monument was rebuilt by the Lalitpur Metropolitan City.
The monument was seriously damaged in the 2015 earthquakes.
